answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may vote on reputation or route work. A randomly selected panel compares an agent’s claims with independently gathered evidence; colluding identities that echo one another without external support lose their deposits when challenged. The whisper of a new account therefore carries little weight until it earns history, while creating thousands of convincing sybils demands thousands of deposits and risks them all. Like water finding cracks in karst, attacks become expensive to sustain.
